title: Head of Support Engineering
description:
ABOUT EXA

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion.

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers Agents, Fortune 500s, and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're a largely SF-based team of ~100 from Harvard, MIT, Meta, Google Research, ex-founders, and dropouts alike. We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We're high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll build and lead Support at Exa: an AI-first, 24/7 support function for every committed customer, worldwide. AI tools like Pylon and AI agents handle the first line; your team of Support Engineers takes on the hard technical problems the AI can't, with the same technical depth as our Forward Deployed Engineers.

You'll also own escalation management: watching the health of every account, largely through AI, and making sure every contraction or churn risk reaches the right people with a clear plan to fix it.

This is a technical leadership role. You hold the same technical bar as your team: you can debug a customer integration, read the code, and open a pull request yourself.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Build the Support team: hire, onboard and lead Support Engineers across regions for 24/7, follow-the-sun coverage

- Build the support system: own our Pylon setup, ticket and SLA tracking, severity levels, automations and the end-of-shift handoffs, so the function runs as efficiently as possible

- Make the AI first line work: decide which tickets the AI resolves and which reach a human, and keep improving the share it resolves without a person

- Own escalations to Engineering: a clear path with full context, and customer follow-up owned by Support until resolution

- Own escalation management: monitor account health across regions, flag every contraction or churn risk to the account team and leadership with requested actions and owners, and follow it until resolved. Escalation management is a duty of your Support Engineers; add dedicated people only if the load requires it

- Partner with the account team (AEs, account managers, FDEs) on at-risk and strategic accounts

- Turn ticket patterns into product feedback, and drive fixes with Product and Engineering

- Report on support health: response and resolution times, customer satisfaction, AI resolution rate, and churn and contraction avoided

REQUIREMENTS

- Several years of hands-on programming experience, at the same level as the Support Engineers you'll hire: you can debug APIs and customer integrations and open pull requests yourself

- 5+ years in technical support, support engineering, SRE or customer engineering, including 2+ years leading a technical support team, ideally at an API, developer-tools or AI company

- Experience building support operations from scratch: tooling, SLAs, severity models, escalation paths and 24/7 coverage

- Strong judgment on automation and AI: you've used AI or automation to scale a support function without lowering quality

- Clear communication with customers, engineers and executives, especially under pressure

YOU MIGHT EXCEL IF YOU...

- Have built or rebuilt a support function at a fast-growing technical company

- Have run Pylon, or a similar support platform, at scale

- Have built with LLMs, RAG or agents

- Care deeply about the problem of organizing the world's knowledge and making it accessible to machines

This is an in-person opportunity in San Francisco We're happy to sponsor international candidates (e.g., STEM OPT, OPT, H1B, O1, E3). In addition to premium healthcare benefits (medical, dental, vision), we also offer fertility benefits and a monthly wellness stipend to all of our employees.

Zepto is building the beating heart of Australia's real-time, account-to-account payments revolution.

A lot of that shift lands on our platform. We're looking for action-oriented people to help build category defining infrastructure. 

Payments is a domain where the details matter. When someone’s wages or a business’s cash flow moves through our platform, it has to arrive correctly, every time, in seconds. Meeting that bar in a regulated industry makes for interesting engineering problems, and as a senior engineer you’ll have real ownership over how we solve them.

We’re a remote-first team that works closely together. Engineers here are trusted to make decisions, encouraged to share their thinking, and supported to grow. That culture is part of why we’ve been named FinTech Organisation of the Year at the Finnies twice.

What you’ll do:

• Build, scale, and maintain high-volume, real-time payment APIs operating in a mission-critical, regulated environment.

• Work across cross-functional teams to design architecture, write RFCs, and ship clean, observable, secure software.

• Collaborate with Platform, Security, and Incident Management teams, participating in a shared on-call rotation.

• Mentor and pair with peers, raising the team's bar for code quality, system design, and engineering practices.

What you’ll bring:

• Strong backend foundations: Deep experience in a backend language and API development. We work in Ruby and Go, and we care more about your engineering than your current language.

• Cloud native architectures: Practical experience on public cloud (preferably AWS), event-driven patterns, Infrastructure as Code, and CI/CD pipelines.

• Scale & reliability mindset: Track record maintaining performance and high availability under heavy transaction loads.

• AI adoption: AI is changing how engineering works, and you're evolving with it. You use tools like Claude Code or Cursor as a core part of delivery, experiment as capabilities improve, while reviewing solutions with rigour and respecting data security boundaries.

• Clear, open communication: You collaborate early with drafts/RFCs and flag risks proactively.

Week 1: You’ll be paired with an onboarding buddy to get familiar with our domains, understand the business context across teams, and ship your first changes to production.

Month 1: You’ll begin to deliver features within your team's domains and review code with real context. You're building relationships across product, engineering and the wider business. You've probably spotted something that we could do better and either fixed it or made the case for prioritising an improvement. 

Month 6: You’ve led a significant feature from idea to production: shaping the requirements with product, writing the RFC, breaking down the work and seeing it land with stakeholders. Why Zepto?

Headquartered in beautiful Byron Bay, Zepto

Our Safety Systems https://openai.com/safety/safety-systems team is at the forefront of OpenAI's mission to build and deploy safe AGI, driving our commitment to AI safety and fostering a culture of trust and transparency.

description:

At Foxelli, we’re building more than e-commerce brands - we’re building a tribe of thoughtful humans: AI enthusiasts, curious builders, and ambitious minds who care about doing meaningful work together. Ten years in, our D2C brands reach millions and generate over $20M annually. Our focus stays simple: create products customers love and a team that actually enjoys building them.

If you love to learn, experiment, think boldly, make decisions, and build things that matter - you’ll feel at home with us.

 
 

THE ROLE

We run AI content production with a team of operators and an internal tool. Output has to go up 10x with the same team. Nobody here knows exactly how, and working that out is the job.

The work

- Study how our operators work today, step by step, and find where the time goes.

- Work out what can be automated and how, then build it. You get no spec and write the plan yourself.

- Take a pipeline that needs a person at every step and make it run end to end: LLM → image/video generation → audio → assembly → QA.

- Solve the hard parts: output consistency across hundreds of generations, retries and fallbacks when model APIs fail, parallel generation, and cost and time per unit.

- Build automated quality control: use vision models to check generated images and video for defects and consistency, and regenerate what fails without a human looking at it.
